Voice

Read articles aloudYour browser's own synthesiser. Free, works offline, and uses the voice you already chose on this machine.
always available
◌

Smart+

Sends the text of the article you are listening to, to OpenAI.
Smart+ voiceA better voice, at the cost of leaving this machine. Off until you turn it on, and unavailable entirely unless the server was started with an API key.
Reading speedHow fast the voice reads. Applied in the player, so it costs nothing and works on audio you have already heard. 1.1 is the default: news read at conversational pace sounds slow.
Summarise before readingTurns a long article into about a minute of spoken summary instead of reading the whole thing. A second request to OpenAI, charged once per article and then cached forever.
Join the stories upNeeds the Smart+ voice above — the segments are written and spoken on the server, so the browser's own voice cannot read them. Rewrites each article as one segment of a continuous broadcast that hands over from the story before it, so a queue sounds like a programme rather than a playlist. Replaces the summary above when both are on. Charged once per pair of articles and then cached.
How it soundsThe narrator's manner. All four say the same facts — they differ in pace, in sentence length, and in how much they tell you what a story is worth. None of them invents anything: an opinion about how much a result matters is allowed, a fact that is not in the article is not.
Opening sting and musicThree notes when the broadcast starts — they fill the pause while the first segment is being written — and a track underneath it afterwards, quiet enough to sit under speech. The music is only downloaded when you first play it, and only the piece you chose. The opening notes are picked at random each broadcast, not from this list — a different one most evenings is expected, not a bug.
Audio is cached on the server, so listening to the same article twice sends it once.

Continuous play

Listening to a list rather than an article
Keep playingWhen an article finishes, mark it read and start the next one down the list. Stops at the end of what's loaded. Works with either voice.
